previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, encephalopathy, and depression was admitted for abdominal pain and confusion. She presented with diffuse stabbing abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, and was found to have elevated liver enzymes, a high lactate, and mild colitis on CT imaging. She was treated with IV fluids, lactulose every two hours, and a brief course of IV antibiotics, later switched to oral ciprofloxacin. Her mental status improved with lactulose, and she was deemed stable for discharge. Blood cultures showed one positive bottle for Corynebacterium, considered a contaminant. She was discharged home with services, on her baseline medications including lactulose, rifaximin, and omeprazole, with instructions to complete a 4-day course of ciprofloxacin and follow up for MRI of the liver and platelet monitoring.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C with hepatic coma

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking part in your medical during your recent 
admission to ___. You came in 
with some confusion.  You had many reasons you might have been 
confused, in part because you were not taking your lactulose as 
frequently as you should causing confusion related to your liver 
disease, and you also were taking more of your psychiatric 
medications than you should, including wellbutrin and your 
seroquel.  Additionally, you have many psychiatric medications 
that can together lead to problems with confusion. You have also 
been drinking, and this can affect your mental status.

You were treated with some medication, and extra lactulose to 
try and get the toxins out of your body. We temporarily stopped 
many of you psychiatric medications as they were likely 
worsening your confusion, and on discharge restarted your 
wellbutrin and trazodone, in discussion with psychiatry.

It is very important that you attend your follow up appointments 
after this hospitalization, with your primary care physician and 
with your psychiatry doctors.

___ you for letting us take part in your medical care. We wish 
you all the best and a speedy recovery.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Care Team
